html:
A Belarusian writer, born in Ukraine in 1948, who builds her books from the voices of ordinary people she interviews. She won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2015.

She trained as a journalist and spent years recording hundreds of people, then cut and arranged their words into a chorus. Her first book, The Unwomanly Face of War, gathered the memories of Soviet women who fought in the Second World War. Zinky Boys was about the Soviet war in Afghanistan, named after the zinc coffins that brought soldiers home. Voices from Chernobyl recorded those who lived through the Chernobyl disaster. Secondhand Time followed people living through the end of the Soviet Union and its aftermath.

Together the books form a history of the Soviet person told from below. Their critical view made her unwelcome to the authorities, and she lived abroad for years. After the disputed 2020 election in Belarus she joined the opposition council and left the country again.
sum: A Belarusian writer, born in Ukraine in 1948, who builds her books from the voices of ordinary people she interviews. She won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2015.
